note: min+gz budgets in bytes, enforced by scripts/size-check.mjs (esbuild bundle via the published exports map, minify, gzip -9). The DEFAULT rule is measured + 2%, and a budget derives from the sweep that set it, never from whatever the `baseline` block below it currently reads. Three gated rows depart from the default and say so in their own note: `core-base` uses the base-successor drift rule (measured + 32 B), `core-base-icu` is frozen at 7680 pending the release captain's post-0.5.0 ratchet, and `core-full-composite` is an owner-signed hard ceiling with no automatic margin at all. `baseline` blocks record the last measured numbers behind a budget — they are evidence, not gates. Entries with pending:true are declared slots a later phase graduates; the gate skips them with the notice in `pendingReason` and they gate nothing until the flag is dropped. Informational entries (no gzipBudgetBytes) are measured and printed, never gated. `external` keeps framework peer deps out of a fixture's bundle so the framework fixtures measure the comvi graph only. `sentinelModules` + `expectSentinels` assert module-graph membership from the esbuild metafile (module IDs, never output text); `node scripts/size-check.mjs --modules` prints the full comvi module list behind those fixtures. framework-slim tier-3 A (.omc/handoffs/fs-tier3.md §1) re-baselined EVERY row in one sweep: `useDefineForClassFields: false` removes the __publicField lowering from all 35 I18n class fields, which is -191 B min+gz on each core entry and -174..-200 B on each framework fixture. No fixture's graph changed, so budgets were recomputed from the new measurements under the unchanged convention (`slim` = measured + 32 B drift, every other gated row = measured + 2%, `full` frozen at the USER-signed 8598 — HISTORICAL, superseded by the 8605 ceiling on `core-full-composite` — and `slim-icu` frozen at 7680). framework-slim tier-3 B (.omc/handoffs/fs-tier3.md §2) then re-baselined every row a SECOND time, for the clean-trio capability extraction (C1 devtools discovery -> the new `@comvi/core/devtools` subpath, C5a tag-grammar entities/escape -> the tags extension, C6 nested-catalog flattening -> the loader capability + the pure `flattenCatalog` export). The slim family drops again; the ROOT and root-host fixtures rise 38-65 B because the root entry, batteries-included at the time, composed all three capabilities back in across chunk boundaries — they still measure 114-135 B BELOW the pre-tier-3 anchor, so gate G5 (root-host fixtures must not regress >2%) is satisfied by improvement, not by margin. framework-slim(perf) then restored the root constructor's first-catalog-write fast path (.omc/handoffs/ctor-perf.md): +6..+11 B min+gz on every core-dependent row (slim 4902 -> 4909, full 8385 -> 8397), 0 over budget. Deliberately NOT re-baselined — absorbing a change this small is exactly what the 32 B slim drift margin and the 2% margin on every other row are for, so budgets and their `baseline` anchors keep deriving from the tier-3 B sweep above. single-entry P1 then re-baselined the core family ONCE more, for the convergence itself: `slim*` rows became `core-base*` (the root IS that host now), `full` became `core-full-composite` (the 0.4 semantics recomposed with `.with(...)` in the parity order), `fw-next-root` became `fw-next-composed-factory` (the published root through a non-exported builder), and two informational `/icu`-installer rows were added. One property of this corpus was measured during that landing and is worth knowing before chasing a byte: a row's gzip figure moves by ~1 B per imported content-hashed chunk name when ANY source edit changes those hash characters, while the minified payload does not change. The core build is deterministic (three consecutive builds produce an identical md5), so such a swing is not flakiness and not weight — it is why `core-full-composite` carries a stated 1 B allowance inside its owner-signed ceiling and nothing else does. ONE AUTHORITATIVE RUN: every `baseline` block in the core family and `fw-next-composed-factory` below is the same landed `node scripts/size-check.mjs` run — `core-base` 5016/13494, `core-base-tags` 5977/16106, `core-base-icu` 5890/15794, `core-base-loader` 6545/18207, `core-base-icu-tags` 6805/18409, `core-base-loader-tags` 7382/20494, `core-full-composite` 8604/23957, `fw-next-composed-factory` 10115/28056. Every other figure in these notes is provenance for a budget or a superseded measurement, and is labelled HISTORICAL where it could be read as current. single-entry P4 then transitioned the NEXT rows without a re-measurement of its own: `fw-next-server-slim-loader` -> `fw-next-server-default-loader` and `fw-next-client-slim-preset` -> `fw-next-client-default` (which also absorbed the deleted two-specifier `fw-next-client-slim` row, one graph that had been reached through two specifiers), each carrying its previous byte anchor forward because the only source change is which name the same base binding is imported under; three NEW next-client rows (`fw-next-client-default-t`, `fw-next-client-icu`, `fw-next-client-full-composite`) ship SENTINEL-GATED with no gzipBudgetBytes and no baseline, so they assert their absences on every run and claim no byte figure until main's P4 sweep records measured + 2% for each. The dropped baseline.modules lists in the two renamed rows were pre-convergence evidence naming core's `comvi-core-slim.js`, which no longer exists; main's sweep repopulates them. single-entry P3 then converged the three remaining wrapper ladders in one sweep (solid ∥ svelte ∥ vue): each package's five root/root-t/slim/slim-t/slim-preset rows collapse into four — `fw-<fw>-default`, `-default-t`, `-icu` and `-full-composite` — measured through the package's ONE published specifier, plus vue's extra informational `fw-vue-default-composed` row, which keeps its preset glue measured rather than claimed. Those rows carry `sentinelModules` + `expectSentinels` and therefore GATE on the single-entry absence claim from the first run, but they deliberately carry NO `gzipBudgetBytes` and NO `baseline`: a budget is measured + 2%, and no converged wrapper graph had been measured when the phase landed. The release captain fills both fields for every such row from ONE authoritative `node scripts/size-check.mjs` run and the rows become fully gated; `pending: true` was deliberately NOT used for them, because it would skip the sentinels too. fixtures.name: fw-nuxt-full-composite

The UPPER BOUND of a nuxt app's comvi graph: the same runtime plugin, useI18n composable and server translation loader as the other two nuxt rows, on a `hostModule` host that composed EVERY capability — ICU, loader, plugin host and devtools discovery. It is NOT the old row re-measured: `fw-nuxt-root` measured the pre-convergence DEFAULT branch, whose construction dragged a composed core in whether the app used it or not, and 0.4 also registered string-API tag syntax ambiently. This is the capability upper bound, not a restoration. Parity ordering inherited from core-full-composite: loader and plugin host first so the nested-catalog flattener is present at ingestion, devtools last so instanceId stays the final public own property, ICU by constructor option because .with(icu()) is pre-ingestion only. <T> is deliberately out of all three nuxt rows so their differences read as capability cost alone; the rich-text seam is measured on the vue ladder, whose component nuxt re-exports verbatim. The two sentinels keep core's tag-registration pair absent — ambient string-API tags are the deliberate explicit-import residual, not part of the capability upper bound. Measured 11648 B min+gz / 34543 B min; byte budget = measured + 2% (11881 B).

fixtures.name: fw-nuxt-server-default-loader

The nuxt SERVER graph on a `hostModule` host that composed the ONE capability SSR needs: runtime plugin + useI18n composable + server translation loader + @comvi/core/loader. Two things did move the graph, which is why the old anchor is not inherited: the fixture switched from the low-level attachLoader to the configured `.with(loader())` installer the docs now recommend, and @comvi/vue/slim collapsed into @comvi/vue, so the baseline modules list re-anchors from comvi-vue-slim.js + chunks/comvi-vue-slim-keys.js to comvi-vue.js + chunks/comvi-vue-keys.js. Five sentinels prove ICU, the plugin host, devtools discovery and core's tag-registration pair are absent from the module graph; the loader subpath is present by construction. Read against fw-nuxt-client-default (same base host, no server utilities, no capability) and fw-nuxt-full-composite (same graph, every capability) — three rows, one construction seam. Measured 10017 B min+gz / 29737 B min; byte budget = measured + 2% (10218 B).

fixtures.name: fw-nuxt-client-default
fixtures.note: RENAMED and RESHAPED in single-entry P4 from `fw-nuxt-client-slim` (framework/nuxt-client-slim.ts, 8013 B min+gz on 2026-08-03). THE DEFAULT nuxt client: runtime plugin + useI18n composable on the base host the generated #build/comvi.host template builds when `hostModule` is unset. The old row measured a bare host reached through the hostModule branch; since the convergence the DEFAULT branch builds exactly that host, so one row states the price — and the fixture now names vue's converged root createI18n instead of the deleted @comvi/vue/slim, which is why the anchor is not inherited. No server loader and no loader capability: nuxt's SSR pass loads and serializes, the client hydrates through addTranslations, a base-host member. The @comvi/core entry left this row's `entry` list because createComviCore is unreachable from a client entry — vue's createI18n is what reaches core's class on this path. Six sentinels prove the four capability subpaths and core's tag-registration pair are absent from the module graph: the default nuxt host composes nothing and the module injects nothing on the app's behalf. Core's BASE entry is present by construction and is deliberately not a sentinel. Measured 8108 B min+gz / 24118 B min; byte budget = measured + 2% (8271 B).
